The agency today announced a rule that updates its regulations to allow greater use of non-animal methods in the development of new drugs and biological products. The change removes language that could be read to require animal studies in cases where other methods, such as cell-based assays and computational models, can provide equivalent information. Officials said the rule reflects advances in science that make it possible to evaluate safety and effectiveness with greater precision. “We want to give developers the flexibility to use the best available tools,” the commissioner said. The rule does not eliminate animal testing where it remains necessary, and sponsors will still be required to demonstrate that alternative methods are scientifically valid. The agency will accept comments for 60 days and plans to issue companion guidance later this year.
